title: Competency Sprint Hire Bundle and Async Interview Scaffold
summary: Lightweight playbook for running a 2-week competency sprint as part of a hiring funnel. Includes a modular candidate bundle (async tasks, live scenario guides), a clear scoring rubric tied to on-the-job signals, and a compact 30-day onboarding checklist to reduce time-to-impact.
purpose: Provide a repeatable, low-variance evaluation path that scales across IC levels and remote candidates while giving hiring managers concrete signals for ramp planning. Reduce interview fatigue by shifting work-like signals to asynchronous tasks and preserve live time for collaboration and culture fit.
scope: Applies to individual contributor engineering roles (IC2-IC5), SWE/infra/serving-runtime tracks initially. Not intended for executive or non-technical hires. This doc covers candidate-facing artifacts, interviewer rubric, score thresholds, and the minimal onboarding package that accompanies an offer.
approach: Run a short competency sprint composed of: 1) takes-home async task (24-48hr window), 2) 60-minute paired design/interview with a hiring manager, 3) 45-minute live debugging/collab session. Score consistently with a four-band rubric mapped to first-90-day success criteria. Feedback captured in a single evaluation form and synthesized by the recruiter for calibration.
interview_scenarios: Scenario A — Latency triage (45m live): Candidate receives a synthetic trace and perf metrics; goal is to form hypotheses, prioritize tests, and propose a remediation plan. Deliverable: one prioritized runbook slide and short verbal plan.

Scenario B — Feature design for batching (60m paired): Design an API/serving approach to enable batching across heterogeneous models with clear tradeoffs (latency vs throughput). Deliverable: architecture sketch + three rollout safety checks.

Scenario C — Async take-home (48h): Small repo with failing tests representing an inference pipeline bug plus a short data-quality investigation. Deliverable: PR with fixes, test, and a 300-500 word rationale.md.

Scenario D — Culture/Collaboration (30m): Behavioral discussion focused on cross-team ops, incident ownership, and postmortem discipline. Look for concrete examples of partnering and communication patterns.
rubric_matrix: Technical Depth: 4=can decompose system-level problems, propose measurable experiments, and implement a working PR; 3=solid design & debugging choices with minor gaps; 2=surface-level tradeoffs and missed edge cases; 1=unable to justify core decisions.
Signal Preservation (Work-like output): 4=async task PR is production-minded (tests, docs, CI); 3=usable code with some gaps; 2=conceptual solution without runnable artifacts; 1=no deliverable.
Ownership & Communication: 4=clear handoffs, runbook artifacts, proactive checkpoints; 3=good communication with occasional missing context; 2=reactive updates; 1=poor clarity.
Collaboration: 4=facilitates pair sessions, mentors interviewer when appropriate; 3=engages well; 2=minimal peer collaboration; 1=poorly aligned with team norms.

Impact Fit (first 90 days): 4=can own a cross-cutting service and reduce unit cost or latency within 90 days; 3=contributes meaningfully with guidance; 2=requires significant onboarding; 1=risk for immediate delivery.
score_thresholds: Accept (strong hire): average >=3.5 across matrix and async task >=3
Accept (hire with plan): average between 3.0-3.49; require 30-60 day focused ramp plan documented in offer appendix
async_interview_templates: Take-home PR template: candidate forks repo, runs tests, opens PR. README contains context, expected outcomes, and explicit timebox (max 5 hours). Include rubric section to set expectations.

Async prompt — 'Pipeline detective': 'Given failing tests and a short sample dataset, identify root cause, add a regression test, and submit a minimal PR. In PR description include hypothesis, steps to reproduce, and one metric you'd monitor in prod.'
Candidate logistics template: clear deadline, recommended environment, CI hints, and a contact for technical blockers. Explicitly state 'do not peer with employees; solo work is required'.
hiring_bundle_components: Candidate packet: one-pager role context, team OKRs, first-90-day goals, and sample production service link
Async repo + small dataset and test harness
Live scenario prompts and interviewer playbook (one pager per scenario)
Recruiter checklist for candidate prep and debrief template
Sample ramp plan template for offers (30/60/90-day goals)
onboarding_checklist: Day 0 — Preboarding: access request sent (VPN, Slack, repo access), welcome doc with team mentor assigned
Day 1 — Orientation: team sync, 1:1 with manager to review first-30-day goals and competency sprint findings
Week 1 — Setup: local dev environment validated, runbook walkthrough, small 'first fix' ticket assigned with buddy
Week 2 — Integration: attend cross-team standups, shadow on-call rotation review, begin real work aligned to ramp plan
Week 4 — Checkpoint: 1:1 with hiring manager + people ops to review progress against 30-day goals and adjust support
Month 2-3 — Impact: deliver first independent PR to prod, own a minor incident postmortem with mentor support
timeline_milestones: Day -7: Requisition approved and competency sprint artifacts published
Day 0: Candidate invited to async task (48h window)
Day 3-7: Live interview loop scheduled and run (includes design & debugging sessions)
Day 8: Debrief and calibration meeting with hiring committee
Day 9-12: Offer drafted with ramp appendix if needed
Day 13-20: Candidate notice period negotiation; aim to close by day 20
acceptance_and_offer_flow: Recruiter compiles a single debrief doc with rubric scores, async artifact links, and recommended ramp plan. HR drafts offer with optional 'focused ramp' appendix when average score is between 3.0 and 3.49. Legal and compensation runs standard checks; people ops confirms final start date and preboarding checklist.
success_metrics: Time-to-offer: target median 14 days from application to offer
Quality-of-hire proxy: % of hires meeting or exceeding 30-day goals = target 80%
Async task completion rate: target 65% of invited candidates complete the async task
operational_notes: Keep async tasks timeboxed to 4-6 hours of candidate effort; longer tasks reduce completion rates.
Rotate scenario prompts quarterly to avoid signal leakage and maintain freshness.
For remote candidates, ensure timezone-friendly scheduling and provide a recorded briefing session for the async task if needed.
open_questions: Should IC4+ candidates get a more senior design partner in the live pairing? (ops impact vs signal consistency)
Do we standardize rewards for completed async tasks (gift card) to improve completion rates?
How tightly should interview scores map to compensation bands for leveling consistency?
notes_to_reviewer: Please review rubric bands for clarity, especially 'Impact Fit' wording. If approved, I'll pilot this bundle with serving-runtime hiring in Q1 and share candidate-level metrics after 12 hires.
